Recent evidence supports text-enhanced recommendation, but does not establish that a scratch-trained ID+text BERT4Rec will improve this benchmark. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.10512v3) jointly learns textual item representations and sequential preferences, but uses pretrained language knowledge and a different training framework. [Dual-View Whitening (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v38i8.28786) finds benefits from reducing pretrained text-embedding anisotropy, while warning that full whitening can damage semantic structure. These results motivate an experiment with a small, randomly initialized title/description encoder jointly integrated into one BERT4Rec network; they do not validate that exact design or justify importing pretrained weights.

Hard negatives require caution: [Enhanced BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) identifies potential positives mislabeled as negatives as a source of misleading gradients. [Negative-sampling experiments (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) also show dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs. A reasonable hypothesis is gradual, mixed random/semi-hard sampling, excluding observed training positives, rather than hardest-only mining. Low user RankMe warrants investigation, not a collapse diagnosis: [NCL-SR (2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/2d2f85c0f93e69cf71f58eebaebb5e8d-Abstract-Conference.html) finds both alignment and uniformity matter, with alignment often more important under sparsity. Compare centered spectra, pairwise similarities and score margins alongside the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Ablate text integration and sampling separately, retaining masked-target training, appended-mask inference and one jointly trained checkpoint per category.
